entries.question: What were new admins worried about at the Invite your team step?

mustClaims.description: New admins were worried (or unsure) that the invites would email the whole team before they were ready; worry, concern or uncertainty wording, not a statement that invites are sent immediately

mustNotClaims.description: Says step 4 (Invite your team) is required or can't be skipped; the wireflow says it can be skipped and nothing in the research makes it required

entries.evidence: Raw session 3: "I guess I'm worried this is going to email my whole team before I'm ready." (the only direct quote). finding:onboarding: admins aren't sure whether invites send immediately or only when the wizard is submitted. Topline: all 3 participants paused at step 4, unsure whether invites send immediately. Journey map: anxious, worried invites are sending before she's ready. Readout: the related hesitation seen in session 3. The wireflow says step 4 can be skipped (audit follow-up §3).

entries.question: Which onboarding steps are required, and which can be skipped?

mustClaims.description: The calendar connection is required or can't be skipped (any step number: the raw notes call it step 2, the canonical flow step 3)
mustClaims.pattern: calendar[^.]{0,80}((?<!not |n't )\brequired|mandatory|can(no|'|’)t be skipped|cannot be skipped|can(no|'|’)t skip|not optional)|((?<!not |n't )\brequired|mandatory)[^.]{0,60}calendar

mustNotClaims.description: Says Basics or Signup can be skipped or is optional (keyed on the step names; a bare step number isn't matched, since the raw notes' "step 2" is the calendar step)
Says every other step is required; only the calendar step is marked required
Says step 4 / Invite your team is required or can't be skipped; the wireflow says it can be skipped and nothing in the research makes it required
mustNotClaims.pattern: (invite your team|invite step|invitation step|step 4)[\"”')]*[^.,;]{0,25}((?<!not |n't )\b(is|are|was) (also )?(required|mandatory)|can(no|'|’)t be skipped)

entries.evidence: user-flows/onboarding-flow: "Step 3 — Connect calendar (now clearly marked required)"; step 4 isn't marked required. finding:onboarding and the readout: step 3 is required though its wording reads as optional. Raw sessions 1–2: participants tried to skip the calendar step and hit the "required" indicator; session 2 calls it "step 2" (the audit's two numbering conventions). Wireflow: "Only step 3 is required … so step 4 can be skipped." No record says Basics or Signup can be skipped. The patterns key on step names, not numbers, because the calendar step is "step 2" in the raw notes and step 3 in the canonical flow. Baseline answer states "Step 2 (Basics) can be skipped" with no citation.

entries.question: What did nurses want from the citations in the prior auth drafts?

mustClaims.description: Inline citations to the specific chart entries or text behind each claim ("show your work")

mustNotClaims.description: Overstates the count: 3 of 4 asked unprompted in v1, and 3 of 4 clicked a citation in v2

entries.evidence: Raw v1 (2025-04-08): participants wanted to see which specific chart entries the AI pulled from, inline; "show your work" was mentioned unprompted by 3 of 4; P17: "Show me where it got that info." Recommendation: inline source citations (chart entry + date) for every claim. Raw v2: 3 of 4 clicked into at least one citation. finding:prior-authorization, the drafting panel component and the v2 service topology restate the requirement.

entries.question: How were sound-alike medication names handled?

mustClaims.description: A distinct sound-alike medication flag (badge), separate from the generic low-confidence underline

mustNotClaims.description: Overstates recognition: 5 of 6 recognized the flag

entries.evidence: Raw 2026-01-13 (GA candidate): sound-alike errors still in 1 of 6 sessions; treat as post-GA monitoring, not a blocker. Raw 2026-02-10 (concept test): a distinct amber pill badge; 5 of 6 recognized it as different from the generic underline; 2 of 6 said it made them trust unflagged lines more; inline placement preferred 5:1. finding:ambient-scribe-post-ga-refinements and finding:ambient-scribe summarize both; the wireframe and thumbnails show the placement.

entries.question: List the onboarding steps in order.

mustClaims.description: The six steps in order: Signup, Basics, Connect calendar, Invite your team, Preferences, Review & finish

mustNotClaims.description: Numbers Basics as step 1 (drops Signup, the miscount the audit traced to stripped list numbers)
Numbers Invite your team as step 3

entries.evidence: user-flows/onboarding-flow is the canonical numbering (audit: "Canonical version chosen"): Step 1 Signup … Step 6 Review & finish. finding:onboarding repeats it in its numbering note; the journey map follows the same order. The raw notes don't list the wizard's steps, so no raw session is required.

entries.question: What does the step 3 wireframe show?

mustClaims.description: Says there is no step 3 wireframe, or that the workspace-setup wireframe is for step 4 (Invite your team)

mustNotClaims.description: Attributes the invite step's wireframe (banner, draft invite list) to step 3

entries.evidence: The only workspace-setup wireframe is "Step 4 (Invite Your Team)" (renamed from workspace-setup-step3.md, audit §5): a "not sent yet" banner and a draft invite list. Step 3 is Connect calendar (user-flows/onboarding-flow); no record has a wireframe for it. The audit logged this question getting a wrong answer from the old filename. No raw session covers wireframes.

entries.question: What is the current session timeout?

mustClaims.description: 10 minutes: IT Security's idle timeout, which it confirmed is not adjustable per feature (Feb 2026)

mustNotClaims.description: Presents the planned, disputed 15-minute re-auth (May 2025) as the current timeout

entries.evidence: Raw 2026-02-17: IT Security confirmed the 10-minute idle timeout is not adjustable per feature ("The timeout window itself is a hard policy constraint"). finding:ambient-scribe-post-ga-refinements and the session-lock user flow give the same 10 minutes but paraphrase it as "fixed", which is stronger than the raw note. The May 2025 IT Security interview has a planned 15-minute re-auth vs clinical ops' 4 hours, unresolved; finding:scope-boundaries puts both on one timeline without saying how the dispute ended (audit: Session timeout).

entries.question: What time period does the ambient scribe GA adoption data cover?

mustClaims.description: The first 4 weeks of the GA-candidate rollout

mustNotClaims.description: Says week 1 or the first week (the topline's old title, audit: Adoption topline title)

entries.evidence: Raw 2026-01-27 dashboard review: "internal analytics dashboard covering the first 4 weeks of GA-candidate rollout." The topline (retitled from "Week 1" in the audit): "Covers the first 4 weeks of GA-candidate rollout, per the 2026-01-27 dashboard review."

entries.question: What percentage of clinicians report burnout?

mustClaims.description: Says the sources give no overall burnout rate
52% of physicians (not "clinicians") name documentation burden as the top contributor to burnout: "52%" or "52 percent" with "physician" and "documentation" in the same answer

mustNotClaims.description: Turns 52% (documentation as physicians' #1 burnout contributor) into a burnout rate

entries.evidence: Raw 2025-09-09 survey: a burnout subscale was used but no burnout rate is reported; documentation burden was the #1 self-selected contributor to burnout among physicians (52%), ahead of patient volume (31%) and meetings (12%); 64% chart after hours. finding:clinician-experience repeats the 52%. The audit logged the model's fabricated "52% report burnout".

entries.question: How aware were staff of the Compass AI initiatives?

mustNotClaims.description: The invented 69%/31% split the audit logged

entries.evidence: Raw 2025-12-02 pulse survey: "Only 34% of non-clinical staff reported being aware Compass AI initiatives were underway at all, versus 71% of clinical staff." finding:rollout-and-change-management repeats it. The audit logged a fabricated "69%/31%" readiness split.
